q8.answer: The merge in the commit transaction updates an existing order only when the staged updated_at is strictly newer than the warehouse row's updated_at (WHEN MATCHED AND s.updated_at > d.updated_at). New order_ids are inserted. Orders has a unique key on order_id, and the replica holds one row per order so staging has one row per order_id per run. A duplicate or older copy is therefore skipped and a repeat run changes nothing.

q9.answer: It is stored in the warehouse table etl_control (one row, pipeline = 'orders', column high_water_mark), since we cannot write to the app database. The value written is hi, the smaller of now() and the replica's pg_last_xact_replay_timestamp(), chosen in step 3. It is written in the final commit transaction, together with the merge and the run-log success update, via a compare-and-set against the HWM value read at the start. If that does not change exactly 1 row, the transaction rolls back.

q10.answer: Each night is loaded into the separate stg_orders table, and orders is changed only by a single warehouse transaction (merge, HWM advance, run-log success, COMMIT). Dashboards read committed data under snapshot isolation, so they see either the old orders or the whole new night. This relies on the warehouse supporting multi-statement transactions with snapshot-isolated readers, which I flagged as an open question I have not verified.

q11.answer: Staging is outside the transaction and each attempt has a new run_id. The retry first runs DELETE FROM stg_orders WHERE run_id = :run_id, so it starts clean. The failed attempt's rows are not used by the retry, and orders was never touched. The HWM is unchanged, so the retry re-reads it and recomputes lo = HWM - 2h and a fresh hi, and extracts rows with lo < updated_at <= hi. That window is the same lower bound as before and a possibly later upper bound.

q12.answer: For each order-creation day (created_at::date) in the last 30 days whose count or checksum differs between replica and warehouse, it re-extracts the whole day from the replica into stg_orders under a recon run id. It applies those rows with the same guarded MERGE (update only if staged updated_at is newer) in one transaction. It does not move the nightly high-water mark, and cannot overwrite newer data.
